value.body: A translator turns written material from one language into another — legal and business documents, websites, apps, books, subtitles and government papers. Translation agencies, localisation companies, publishers, media houses and government offices hire translators, and many work freelance.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.A. or M.A. in the language(s)
items.note: A translation diploma or certificate helps

items.label: Common tools
items.value: CAT tools, translation memory, word processors

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start with agency or freelance work, taking a test translation. A strong command of both languages and a few sample translations matter more than the degree title.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is often project-based, and freelance income can be uneven.
Machine translation now handles first drafts in many fields; human post-editing is a growing share of work.
Specialising (legal, medical, technical, subtitles) widens the work available.
